checks.method: Read MeetingDefect.lean and independently expanded exact trace counts tj=number of members meeting anchorR in j points. Enumerated count vectors with total61,t1<=40,t4=1 and incidence total<=66.
checks.observation: Because families contain distinct four-sets and R belongs to H, t4=1 exactly. The identity D=2|M|-t1+t3+2t4 gives2|M|+2<=D+40. All7,393 feasible numerical trace vectors have at least9 disjoint rows; the boundary vector(t0,t1,t2,t3,t4)=(9,40,11,0,1) has incidence66. This validates the integer threshold while making no family-realizability claim. Omitting the anchor would invalidate the +2 step, but both manuscript and formal theorem explicitly retain it.
checks.scope: Challenge to the +2 defect and nine-completion threshold

checks.method: Inspected TwoStarBridge.two_star_degree_partition and residual_degree_bounds against the two-star proof text.
checks.observation: The formal degree partition uses the explicit no-member-containing-both-centers hypothesis, so the five x-star and five y-star contributions are disjoint even at an overlap point. It also proves link-support points differ from both centers before applying the other-point degree cap19. Thus the residual caps14 and9 are justified; an overlapping-star counterexample would violate a stated hypothesis. These are structural identities and use no diagnostic45 output.
checks.scope: Challenge to overlap degree loss and outside-point assumptions

content.summary: Skeptical checks found no off-by-one error in the nine-completion argument and no double subtraction in the two-star residual degree budgets. The closed-neighborhood anchor is essential and present; the noncooccurrence hypothesis supplies the disjoint partition needed for19-5-5=9. The revised singleton-trace explanation agrees with the inherited bound used by the frozen source.
